blocks.title: Introduction and description of results
blocks.content:
This paper is about knots which are transverse to the standard tight contact structure in
R3, and about the ways in which topological information about braids can be used to
learn new things about these ‘transversal knots’. Our approach to contact topology had
its origins in the foundational paper of D Bennequin [2]. The results in this paper are
direct outgrowths of our work on the Markov Theorem without Stabilization (MTWS)
[6].
A knot in oriented R3 is the image X of an oriented circle S1 under a smooth
embedding eW S1 ! R3. Viewing S3 as R3 [ 1, we also can think of X as being a

The main result of this paper is a negative answer to the question: are all transversal
knot types transversally simple? An explicit inﬁnite family of examples is given of
closed 3–braids that deﬁne transversal knot types that are not transversally simple.
The method of proof is topological and indirect.
